metadata.title: Parallelized Stochastic Gradient Descent
metadata.authors: Martin A. Zinkevich, Markus Weimer, Alex Smola, Lihong Li
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Per-example loss $c^i(w)$ and overall risk $c(w)$
nodes.statement: For convex losses $c^i: \ell_2 \to [0,\infty)$, $c^i(w) = \tfrac{\lambda}{2}\|w\|^2 + L(x^i,y^i,w\cdot x^i)$, and the overall risk is $c(w) = \tfrac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m c^i(w)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Defines the regularized per-example loss and the average risk to be minimized.

nodes.name: Lipschitz continuity
nodes.statement: $f: X \to \mathbb{R}$ is Lipschitz continuous with constant $L$ w.r.t. distance $d$ if $|f(x)-f(y)| \leq L\, d(x,y)$ for all $x,y \in X$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard Lipschitz continuity definition.

nodes.name: Holder continuity
nodes.statement: $f$ is Holder continuous with constant $L$ and exponent $\alpha$ if $|f(x)-f(y)| \leq L\, d^{\alpha}(x,y)$ for all $x,y \in X$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard Holder continuity definition.

nodes.name: Lipschitz seminorm $\|f\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}$
nodes.statement: $\|f\|_{\mathrm{Lip}} := \inf\{ l : |f(x)-f(y)| \leq l\, d(x,y) \text{ for all } x,y \in X \}$, the smallest Lipschitz constant.
nodes.statement_clean: The infimum of valid Lipschitz constants.

nodes.name: Holder seminorm $\|f\|_{\mathrm{Lip}_\alpha}$
nodes.statement: For $\alpha \geq 1$: $\|f\|_{\mathrm{Lip}_\alpha} := \inf\{ l : |f(x)-f(y)| \leq l\, d^{\alpha}(x,y) \text{ for all } x,y \in X \}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Holder analogue of the Lipschitz seminorm.

nodes.name: Contraction mapping
nodes.statement: For a metric space $(M,d)$, $f: M \to M$ is a contraction mapping if $\|f\|_{\mathrm{Lip}} < 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: A self-map of a metric space whose Lipschitz constant is strictly less than 1.

nodes.name: SGD update map $\phi^i$
nodes.statement: $\phi^i(w) := w - \eta \nabla c^i(w)$, the stochastic gradient step on the $i$-th example.
nodes.statement_clean: The single-step SGD update viewed as a map on weight vectors.

nodes.name: Critical learning rate $\eta^*$
nodes.statement: $\eta^* := \min_i (\|x^i\|^2 c^* + \lambda)^{-1}$, the upper bound on $\eta$ ensuring contraction.
nodes.statement_clean: The largest learning rate guaranteeing the SGD update is a contraction.

nodes.name: Wasserstein metric $W_z$
nodes.statement: For a Radon space $(M,d)$ and distributions $X,Y \in P(M,d)$: $W_z(X,Y) = \inf_{\gamma \in \Gamma(X,Y)} \big( \int_{x,y} d^z(x,y)\, d\gamma(x,y) \big)^{1/z}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The Monge-Kantorovich-Wasserstein earth-mover distance of order $z$.

nodes.name: Lifted distribution map $p$
nodes.statement: Given $\phi: M \to M$, define $p: P(M,d) \to P(M,d)$ by applying $\phi$ pointwise: $X'(E) = X(\phi^{-1}(E))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Pushforward of a distribution under a pointwise map.

nodes.name: Mixture SGD operator $p^*$ and parameter distribution $D_\eta^t$
nodes.statement: $p^* = \tfrac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m p^i$ is the one-step stochastic operation; $D_\eta^t = p^*(D_\eta^{t-1})$ is the parameter distribution after $t$ SGD steps starting from $D_\eta^0$.
nodes.statement_clean: The averaged update operator and its iterates on distributions.

nodes.name: Strong convexity
nodes.statement: $c$ is $\lambda$-strongly convex if $\tfrac{\lambda}{2}(y-x)^2 + \nabla c(x)\cdot(y-x) + c(x) \leq c(y)$ for all $x,y \in M$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard strong convexity inequality.

nodes.name: Relative standard deviation $\sigma_X^c$
nodes.statement: $\sigma_X^c = \sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(X-c)^2]}$; with $\sigma_X = \sigma_X^{\mu_X}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Root-mean-square deviation of $X$ from a reference point $c$.

nodes.name: Lipschitz-bounded loss gradient
nodes.statement: $\|L(x,y,y')\|_{\mathrm{Lip}} \leq G$ as a function of $y'$ for all data $(x,y) \in X \times Y$ and all $w$ in a suitably chosen (often compact) domain.
nodes.statement_clean: The loss gradient is uniformly bounded by $G$.

nodes.name: SGD (single-machine inner routine)
nodes.statement: Single-machine stochastic gradient descent over $\{c^1,\ldots,c^m\}$ with fixed learning rate $\eta$ for $T$ steps.
nodes.statement_clean: Plain fixed-rate SGD over $T$ random index draws.
nodes.pseudocode: for t=1..T: draw j uniformly from {1..m}; $w_t \leftarrow w_{t-1} - \eta \partial_w c^j(w_{t-1})$; return $w_T$.

nodes.name: ParallelSGD
nodes.statement: Run SGD independently on $k$ clients and average the resulting weight vectors.
nodes.statement_clean: Single-pass averaging of $k$ independent SGD runs.
nodes.pseudocode: for i=1..k in parallel: $v_i =$ SGD($\{c^1,\ldots,c^m\}$, $T$, $\eta$, $w_0$); return $v = \tfrac{1}{k}\sum_i v_i$.

nodes.name: SimuParallelSGD
nodes.statement: MapReduce-friendly variant: partition data across $k$ machines, run a local SGD pass on each, average the results.
nodes.statement_clean: Partition-then-average single-pass parallel SGD.
nodes.pseudocode: Define $T = \lfloor m/k \rfloor$; partition examples into $k$ blocks of size $T$; for each machine $i$ in parallel: shuffle local data, $w_{i,0}=0$, for $t=1..T$: $w_{i,t} \leftarrow w_{i,t-1} - \eta \partial_w c_{i,t}(w_{i,t-1})$; return $v = \tfrac{1}{k}\sum_i w_{i,T}$.

nodes.name: Partition data across machines
nodes.statement: Define $T = \lfloor m/k \rfloor$ and randomly partition the examples, giving $T$ examples to each machine.

nodes.name: Local shuffle and initialize $w_{i,0}=0$
nodes.statement: Each machine $i$ shuffles its local data and sets $w_{i,0} = 0$.

nodes.name: Local SGD loop
nodes.statement: For $t = 1,\ldots,T$ on machine $i$: read local example $c_{i,t}$ and update $w_{i,t} \leftarrow w_{i,t-1} - \eta \partial_w c_i(w_{i,t-1})$.

nodes.name: Aggregate by averaging
nodes.statement: Aggregate from all computers $v = \tfrac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^k w_{i,T}$ and return $v$.

nodes.name: Banach's Fixed Point Theorem
nodes.statement: If $(M,d)$ is a non-empty complete metric space, then any contraction mapping $f$ on $(M,d)$ has a unique fixed point $x^* = f(x^*)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Contractions on complete metric spaces have unique fixed points.
assumptions: $(M,d)$ is a non-empty complete metric space
$f: M \to M$ is a contraction mapping
conclusions: $f$ has a unique fixed point $x^* = f(x^*)$

nodes.name: Linear convergence of fixed-point iteration
nodes.statement: The sequence $x_t = f(x_{t-1})$ converges linearly with $d(x^*, x_t) \leq \|f\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}^t\, d(x_0, x^*)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Banach iteration converges geometrically.

nodes.name: SGD step is a contraction (Lemma 3)
nodes.statement: Let $c^* \geq \|\partial_{\hat y} L(x^i,y^i,\hat y)\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}$. If $\eta \leq (\|x^i\|^2 c^* + \lambda)^{-1}$, then the update $\phi^i$ is a contraction in $\ell_2$ with constant $1 - \eta\lambda$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sufficiently small $\eta$ makes the per-example gradient step a contraction.
assumptions: $L$ has Lipschitz gradient with constant $c^*$ in $\hat y$
conclusions: $\phi^i$ is a contraction in $\ell_2$ with Lipschitz constant $1 - \eta\lambda$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: Decompose $w$ into components parallel and perpendicular to $x^i$, bound each component, and show the combined map shrinks distances by $1-\eta\lambda$.

nodes.name: Rewrite update via $u(z)$
nodes.statement: Define $u(z) = \partial_z L(y^i, z)$, which is increasing and Lipschitz with constant $c^*$. Then $\phi^i(w) = (1-\eta\lambda)w - \eta u(w\cdot x^i)x^i$.

nodes.name: Decompose $w = w_\parallel + w_\perp$
nodes.statement: Split $w$ into the component $w_\parallel$ along $x^i$ and $w_\perp$ orthogonal. Then $\phi^i(w)_\perp = (1-\eta\lambda)w_\perp$ and $\phi^i(w)_\parallel = (1-\eta\lambda)w_\parallel - \eta u(w_\parallel\cdot x^i)x^i$.

nodes.name: Bound parallel component
nodes.statement: Using $|u(\alpha(w))-u(\alpha(v))| \leq c^*|\alpha(w)-\alpha(v)|$ and $\eta \leq (\beta^2 c^* + \lambda)^{-1}$, derive $d(\phi^i(w)_\parallel,\phi^i(v)_\parallel) \leq (1-\eta\lambda) d(w_\parallel,v_\parallel)$.

nodes.name: Combine components
nodes.statement: Since $d(w,v) = \sqrt{d^2(w_\parallel,v_\parallel) + d^2(w_\perp,v_\perp)}$, conclude $d(\phi^i(w),\phi^i(v)) \leq (1-\eta\lambda) d(w,v)$.

nodes.name: Pointwise contraction lifts to distributions (Lemma 5)
nodes.statement: Given a metric space $(M,d)$ and a contraction $\phi$ on $(M,d)$ with constant $c$, the induced map $p$ on $(P(M,d), W_z)$ is a contraction with the same constant $c$.
nodes.statement_clean: Lifting a contraction pointwise yields a contraction in Wasserstein.
assumptions: $\phi$ is a contraction on $(M,d)$ with constant $c$
conclusions: $p$ is a contraction on $(P(M,d), W_z)$ with constant $c$

nodes.name: Mixture of contractions is a contraction (Lemma 6)
nodes.statement: If $p_1,\ldots,p_k$ are contractions with constants $c_1,\ldots,c_k$ w.r.t. $W_z$ and $a_i \geq 0$ with $\sum_i a_i = 1$, then $p = \sum_i a_i p_i$ is a contraction with constant at most $(\sum_i a_i c_i^z)^{1/z}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Convex mixtures of Wasserstein contractions remain contractions.
conclusions: $p = \sum_i a_i p_i$ is a contraction with constant $\leq (\sum_i a_i c_i^z)^{1/z}$

nodes.name: Uniform contraction constant for mixtures (Corollary 7)
nodes.statement: If $c_i \leq c$ for all $i$, then $p = \sum_i a_i p_i$ is a contraction with constant at most $c$.
nodes.statement_clean: Mixture inherits the worst component constant.

nodes.name: SGD operator is a contraction with stationary distribution (Theorem 8)
nodes.statement: For any $z \in \mathbb{N}$, if $\eta \leq \eta^*$, then $p^*$ is a contraction on $(M, W_z)$ with rate $1-\eta\lambda$; there is a unique fixed point $D_\eta^*$ with $p^*(D_\eta^*) = D_\eta^*$, and if $w_0=0$ a.s. then $W_z(D_\eta^0, D_\eta^*) = G/\lambda$ and $W_z(D_\eta^T, D_\eta^*) \leq (G/\lambda)(1-\eta\lambda)^T$.
nodes.statement_clean: Mixture SGD operator contracts in Wasserstein and converges geometrically to a unique stationary distribution.
conclusions: $p^*$ is a contraction on $(M, W_z)$ with rate $1-\eta\lambda$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 8
nodes.statement: Combine Lemma 3, Lemma 5, and Corollary 7 to get the contraction rate; bound $\|w_t\|$ by $G/\lambda$ via Theorem 44; apply Corollary 2 (Banach iteration) for the geometric convergence rate.

nodes.name: Bias of stationary mean (Theorem 9)
nodes.statement: $c(\mathbb{E}_{w \in D_\eta^*}[w]) - \min_{w \in \mathbb{R}^n} c(w) \leq 2\eta G^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: The cost at the stationary mean is within $2\eta G^2$ of the optimum.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 9
nodes.statement: Use a regret-minimization argument with potential $\Phi_t = (w_{t+1}-w^*)^2/(2\eta)$ to bound regret by $T\eta M^2/2 + D^2/(2\eta)$, then apply Cesaro limits and Jensen.

nodes.name: Online-to-batch via potential
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 46: regret of fixed-rate SGD on convex losses bounded by $T\eta M^2/2 + D^2/(2\eta)$.

nodes.name: Cesaro limit of regret bound
nodes.statement: Using Theorem 48, $\lim_{T\to\infty} \tfrac{1}{T}\mathbb{E}[R_T] \geq \mathbb{E}_{w \in D_\eta^*}[c(w)] - \min_w c(w)$. Combine to get $\eta M^2/2 \geq \mathbb{E}_{w \in D_\eta^*}[c(w)] - \min_w c(w)$.

nodes.name: Jensen at the mean
nodes.statement: By Jensen (since $c$ convex), $c(\mathbb{E}[w]) \leq \mathbb{E}[c(w)]$, so $c(\mathbb{E}_{w \in D_\eta^*}[w]) - \min_w c(w) \leq \eta M^2/2$. Substitute $M = 2G$ (Corollary 45) to get $2\eta G^2$.

nodes.name: Variance of stationary distribution (Theorem 10)
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}_{w \in D_\eta^*}[(w-w^*)^2] \leq \tfrac{4\eta G^2}{(2-\eta\lambda)\lambda}$, i.e. $O(\eta G^2/\lambda)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Stationary distribution concentrates near the optimum with variance $O(\eta G^2/\lambda)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 10
nodes.statement: Embed SGD into an infinite-horizon average-reward MDP with reward $w^2$; solve the supremum Bellman equation explicitly (Theorem 65); apply Theorem 66 with $r=\eta\lambda$ and $M=2\eta G$.

nodes.name: Cost gap from a near-mean distribution (Theorem 11)
nodes.statement:
Given $c$ with $\|c\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}, \|
abla c\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}$ bounded and bounded $\sigma_D$, for any $v$: $\mathbb{E}_{w \in D}[c(w)] - \min_w c(w) \leq W_2(v,D)\sqrt{2\|
abla c\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}(c(v)-\min_w c(w))} + 	frac{\|
abla c\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}}{2}W_2(v,D)^2 + (c(v)-\min_w c(w))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bounds the expected suboptimality of a distribution by its $W_2$-distance to a reference point and the reference's suboptimality.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 11
nodes.statement: Decompose $c(w') - c(v)$ into linear and quadratic remainders via Taylor with Lipschitz $\nabla c$, then bound each piece using extended Kantorovich-Rubinstein (Theorem 24) and Lemma 13.

nodes.name: Main bound for ParallelSGD (Theorem 12)
nodes.statement: If $\eta \leq \eta^*$ and $T = \tfrac{\ln k - (\ln \eta + \ln \lambda)}{2\eta\lambda}$, then $\mathbb{E}_{w \in D_\eta^{T,k}}[c(w)] - \min_w c(w) \leq \tfrac{8\eta G^2}{\sqrt{k}\lambda}\sqrt{\|\nabla c\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}} + \tfrac{8\eta G^2 \|\nabla c\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}}{k\lambda} + 2\eta G^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Final convergence guarantee for parallel SGD with $k$ machines and $T$ local steps.
conclusions: $\mathbb{E}_{w \in D_\eta^{T,k}}[c(w)] - \min_w c(w) \leq \tfrac{8\eta G^2}{\sqrt{k}\lambda}\sqrt{\|\nabla c\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}} + \tfrac{8\eta G^2 \|\nabla c\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}}{k\lambda} + 2\eta G^2$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 12
nodes.statement: Combine variance reduction by averaging $k$ machines (Theorem 34), the bias decay $G(1-\eta\lambda)^T/\lambda$ from Theorem 8, the choice of $T$ to balance bias and variance, and apply Theorem 11 with $v = \mu_{D_\eta^*}$ and Theorem 9.

nodes.name: Variance shrinks by $\sqrt{k}$
nodes.statement: By Theorem 34, $\mu_{D_\eta^{T,k}} = \mu_{D_\eta^T}$ and $\sigma_{D_\eta^{T,k}} \leq \sigma_{D_\eta^T}/\sqrt{k}$.

nodes.name: Bias decays geometrically
nodes.statement: By Corollary 71, $d(\mu_{D_\eta^{T,k}}, \mu_{D_\eta^*}) \leq (G/\lambda)(1-\eta\lambda)^T$ and $\sigma_{D_\eta^{T,k}} \leq \sigma_{D_\eta^{T,k}}^{\mu_{D_\eta^*}}$ controlled similarly.

nodes.name: Choose $T$ to balance terms
nodes.statement: Setting $T = (\ln k - \ln\eta - \ln\lambda)/(2\eta\lambda)$ gives $\sigma_{D_\eta^{T,k}}^{\mu_{D_\eta^*}} \leq 4\sqrt{\eta} G/\sqrt{k\lambda}$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 11 and Theorem 9
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 11 with $v = \mu_{D_\eta^*}$ and substitute $c(\mu_{D_\eta^*}) - \min_w c(w) \leq 2\eta G^2$ from Theorem 9 to obtain the stated three-term bound.

nodes.name: Gradient norm bound for convex Lipschitz-gradient $f$ (Lemma 13)
nodes.statement: If $f$ convex with $\nabla f$ Lipschitz with constant $H$ and $x^*$ minimizes $f$, then $\|\nabla f(x)\|^2 \leq 2H[f(x) - f(x^*)]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Gradient magnitude bounded by suboptimality times smoothness.

nodes.name: Strongly convex centering (Lemma 14)
nodes.statement: If $c$ is $\lambda$-strongly convex with minimizer $x^*$, then $f(x) = c(x) - \tfrac{\lambda}{2}(x-x^*)^2$ is convex and $x^*$ minimizes $f$.
nodes.statement_clean: Subtracting the strongly-convex quadratic at the minimizer yields a convex function with the same minimizer.

nodes.name: Strongly convex contraction in distance (Lemma 15)
nodes.statement:
If $c$ is $\lambda$-strongly convex with minimizer $x^*$, $
abla c$ is Lipschitz, $f(x) = c(x) - 	frac{\lambda}{2}(x-x^*)^2$, $\eta < (\lambda + \|
abla f\|_{\mathrm{Lip}})^{-1}$, $\eta < 1$, then for all $x$: $d(x - \eta
abla c(x), x^*) \leq (1-\eta\lambda) d(x, x^*)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Gradient step contracts toward optimum with rate $1-\eta\lambda$.

nodes.name: Contraction toward optimum for regularized loss (Lemma 16)
nodes.statement:
Given convex $L$ with Lipschitz $
abla L$ and $c(x) = 	frac{\lambda}{2}x^2 + L(x)$, if $\eta < (\lambda + \|
abla L\|_{\mathrm{Lip}})^{-1}$, then $d(x - \eta
abla c(x), x^*) \leq (1-\eta\lambda) d(x, x^*)$ for all $x$.
nodes.statement_clean: Lemma 15 specialized to the regularized-loss form.

nodes.name: Pairwise contraction of gradient step (Theorem 17)
nodes.statement:
Given convex $L$ with Lipschitz $
abla L$ and $c(x) = 	frac{\lambda}{2}x^2 + L(x)$, if $\eta < (\lambda + \|
abla L\|_{\mathrm{Lip}})^{-1}$, then $d(x - \eta
abla c(x), y - \eta
abla c(y)) \leq (1-\eta\lambda) d(x,y)$ for all $x,y$.
nodes.statement_clean: Pairwise contraction property of one batch gradient step.

nodes.name: Kantorovich-Rubinstein theorem (Theorem 22)
nodes.statement: If $(M,d)$ is a separable metric space, then for any distributions $P,Q$, $W_1(P,Q) = \sup_{\|f\|_{\mathrm{Lip}} \leq 1} (\int f\, dP - \int f\, dQ)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Dual representation of the $W_1$ distance.

nodes.name: Means closer than $W_1$ (Corollary 23)
nodes.statement: If $d$ is Euclidean, then $d(\mu_P, \mu_Q) \leq W_1(P, Q)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Means of distributions are no farther than $W_1$ distance.

nodes.name: Higher-order Kantorovich-Rubinstein extension (Theorem 24)
nodes.statement: For any $i \geq 1$ and $f$ with $\|f\|_{\mathrm{Lip}_i}$ bounded, and distributions $X,Y$: $|\mathbb{E}_{x \in X}[f(x)] - \mathbb{E}_{y \in Y}[f(y)]| \leq \|f\|_{\mathrm{Lip}_i}(W_i(X,Y))^i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Generalization of Kantorovich-Rubinstein to Holder-$i$ functions.

nodes.name: Variance of an i.i.d. average (Theorem 34)
nodes.statement: If $X^1,\ldots,X^k$ are i.i.d. random vectors over $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $A = \tfrac{1}{k}\sum_i X^i$, then $\mu_A = \mu_{X^1}$ and $\sigma_A \leq \sigma_{X^1}/\sqrt{k}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard $1/\sqrt{k}$ variance reduction by averaging.

nodes.name: Boundedness of SGD iterates (Theorem 44)
nodes.statement: If $w_0 = 0$, $\lambda \leq 1$, and $0 \leq \eta \leq 1/\lambda$, then $\|w_t\| \leq G/\lambda$ for all SGD iterates.
nodes.statement_clean: SGD iterates remain in a ball of radius $G/\lambda$.

nodes.name: Online regret bound for fixed-rate SGD (Theorem 46)
nodes.statement: For convex losses $\{c_t\}$ on domain $F$ of diameter $D$ with gradient bound $M$, fixed-rate SGD has regret $R_T \leq \tfrac{T\eta M^2}{2} + \tfrac{D^2}{2\eta}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard fixed-rate online gradient descent regret.

nodes.name: Closed-form Bellman solution (Theorem 65)
nodes.statement: The solution to the Bellman equation $V_\gamma^*(w) = w^2 + \gamma \sup_{a \in A(w)} \mathbb{E}[V_\gamma^*(a)]$ is $V_\gamma^*(w) = \tfrac{1}{1 - \gamma(1-r)^2}\big(w^2 + \tfrac{\gamma}{1-\gamma}M^2\big)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Closed-form value function for the auxiliary contractive MDP.

nodes.name: Stationary $\mathbb{E}[w^2]$ bound (Theorem 66)
nodes.statement: If $p$ is a contraction on $(P(S,d),W_z)$ with $p(I_w) \in A(w)$, then there is a unique fixed point $D^*$ and $\mathbb{E}_{w \in D^*}[w^2] \leq \tfrac{M^2}{(2-r)r}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bellman value bound transferred to any contractive stationary distribution.

nodes.name: Stochastic gradient update with $L_2$ regularization
nodes.statement: $w_{t+1} = w_t - \eta(\lambda w_t + \nabla f^i(w_t))$, the SGD update for $c^i(w) = \tfrac{\lambda}{2}w^2 + L(y^i, w \cdot x^i)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Update equation used throughout the analysis.

nodes.name: Email-system experiments with Huber and squared loss
nodes.statement: Train SimuParallelSGD on a proprietary email dataset with $3{,}189{,}235$ time-stamped instances, $785{,}751{,}531$ hashed binary features (218-dim hashed space, ~313 features/instance, sparsity 0.0012); compare $1$, $10$, $100$ machines under Huber and squared loss with $\lambda \in \{10^{-3}, 10^{-6}\}$ and $\eta = 10^{-3}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical evaluation showing parallelization reduces wall-clock time and helps more when $\lambda$ is small.

nodes.name: Regularized risk minimization
nodes.statement: Find $w^* = \arg\min_w c(w)$ where $c(w) = \tfrac{1}{m}\sum_i c^i(w)$ and $c^i(w) = \tfrac{\lambda}{2}\|w\|^2 + L(x^i, y^i, w \cdot x^i)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Convex regularized empirical risk minimization solved by ParallelSGD.

nodes.name: Discussion of the bound
nodes.statement: The bound has no explicit dependence on $m$; modulo logs, with $G=1, \|\nabla c\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}=1$, $\kappa = 1/\lambda$, and target $\rho = \eta$, ParallelSGD needs $k = 1/\lambda$ machines running for $1/(\eta\lambda)$ time, matching the [2] iteration count modulo logs but with a $1/\lambda$ wall-clock speedup. Halving $\eta$ and roughly doubling $T$ halves the error; if $k > \|\nabla c\|_{\mathrm{Lip}}/\lambda$ the $\eta G^2$ term dominates.
nodes.statement_clean: Discusses how the bound translates to wall-clock speedups versus baseline SGD analyses.

nodes.name: Comparison to prior parallel-SGD approaches
nodes.statement: Prior approaches: distributed subgradient [3,9] (high IO, many MapReduce passes), distributed convex solver [7] (single MapReduce, but full batch solver per machine and only variance reduction), multicore SGD [5] (low-latency only). This paper: high latency tolerance, MapReduce, low IO, linear scalability.
nodes.statement_clean: Positions ParallelSGD against [3,9], [7], and [5] in a feature table.
